instruction:
Independent verification task in the JS repo at /luxon. Do NOT edit any file in /luxon (treat the repo as read-only); put all scratch files in /tmp. Use bash and read_file.

CONTEXT: a fix was just applied to /luxon/src/duration.js: the `casualMatrix.quarters` entry was missing the `seconds` conversion, and `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` was added between `minutes` and `milliseconds`. Verify this fix and that nothing regressed.

1) `cd /luxon && git diff src/duration.js` — report the diff verbatim and confirm it is ONLY the added `seconds` line (no other change in that file).
2) Write /tmp/verify5.js and run it with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/verify5.js`. It must import `const { Duration } = require("/luxon/src/luxon.js");` and, for every ordered pair (a, b) of the units ["years","quarters","months","weeks","days","hours","minutes","seconds","milliseconds"] (including a === b), build `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1 })`, call `.normalize()`, and check that (i) the result is valid, (ii) `.as("milliseconds")` is finite, and (iii) `.as("milliseconds")` equals the original duration's `.as("milliseconds")` within a relative tolerance of 1e-9. Print every failure and a total failure count. Do the same loop again with `{ conversionAccuracy: "longterm" }` as the second argument to fromObject. Also print `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).as("seconds")`.
3) Also check the reverse direction and shiftTo: print `Duration.fromObject({ seconds: 1 }).shiftTo("quarters").toObject()`, `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).shiftTo("seconds").toObject()`, and `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 30 }).normalize().toObject()`.
4) Run the FULL test suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 25`. Expected: 894 tests, 892 passing, 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French-locale `DateTime#toFormat('FFF')` and `('FFFF')` without seconds), 55 suites with 1 failing suite. Report exact numbers and any failing test whose name is NOT one of those two (a regression). Also run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -n 20`.
5) `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` — report it; there should be no untracked files inside the repo.

REPORT: the duration.js diff, every failure line and the two failure counts from step 2, the step 3 values, the full-suite and duration-suite numbers, and the git status. Include raw output.

You are fixing a bug in the JS repo at /luxon (the luxon date library). Do everything yourself with bash/read_file/edit_file; do not ask questions. Never modify test files or any file other than the one named below.

GOAL: fix the bug in /luxon/src/duration.js in the `casualMatrix` constant (around lines 30-59). Its `quarters` entry is missing the `seconds` conversion, so `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize()` (and any quarters<->seconds conversion) produces NaN. The `accurateMatrix` quarters entry has the corresponding `seconds` line, which confirms the intended shape.

CURRENT (buggy) CODE:

      quarters: {
        months: 3,
        weeks: 13,
        days: 91,
        hours: 91 * 24,
        minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,
        milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
      },

FIX: add the missing line so it reads exactly:

      quarters: {
        months: 3,
        weeks: 13,
        days: 91,
        hours: 91 * 24,
        minutes: 91 * 24 * 60,
        seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,
        milliseconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
      },

Change nothing else anywhere in the repo (note: other agents are concurrently editing src/impl/util.js and src/datetime.js — do NOT touch those files).

VERIFICATION (do all of it):
1) BEFORE the edit, write /tmp/bug5_before.js and run it with `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/bug5_before.js`. It must import `const { Duration } = require("/luxon/src/luxon.js");`, then for every ordered pair (a, b) of the units ["years","quarters","months","weeks","days","hours","minutes","seconds","milliseconds"] build `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1 })`, call `.normalize()`, and check that the normalized duration is valid and that its millisecond value is finite and equals the original duration's millisecond value (use `.as("milliseconds")`; compare with a relative tolerance of 1e-9). Print every failing pair with the got/expected numbers, plus a total failure count. Also print `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}).normalize().toObject()` and `.as("seconds")` explicitly.
2) Apply the fix.
3) Re-run the script: the failure count must be 0 and the explicit values must be finite ({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 } normalizes to quarters 1 with 1 second kept as a fractional/rolled value — just report what it prints, it must not be NaN).
4) Also verify with the accurate conversion accuracy: repeat the pair loop with `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1 }, { conversionAccuracy: "longterm" })` and report the failure count (must be 0).
5) Run the FULL test suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 25`. Expected: 894 tests, 892 passing, 2 pre-existing failures in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (French-locale `DateTime#toFormat('FFF')` and `('FFFF')` without seconds) and 55 suites with 1 failing suite. Report the exact numbers and any test that fails whose name is NOT one of those two (that would be a regression). Also run `cd /luxon && npx jest test/duration 2>&1 | tail -n 20`.
6) `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` must show ` M src/duration.js` (plus possibly ` M src/impl/util.js` and ` M src/datetime.js` from the concurrent agents — that is expected). No untracked files inside the repo; keep scratch files in /tmp.

REPORT: the before/after failure counts and explicit values, the longterm-accuracy result, the full-suite and duration-suite results, and the git status output. Include raw command output.

URGENT, do the EDIT FIRST, before any verification. Repo /luxon (JS luxon date library). Do not modify test files.

STEP 1 (do this immediately): in /luxon/src/duration.js add `quarters: 4,` as the FIRST entry inside BOTH `years` blocks — the one in `casualMatrix` (currently starting `years: {` with `months: 12,`) and the one in `accurateMatrix` (currently starting `years: {` with `months: 12,`). Result must be:

      years: {
        quarters: 4,
        months: 12,
        ...

in both places (the accurateMatrix years block keeps its `weeks: daysInYearAccurate / 7` etc. untouched). This completes the conversion matrix: `matrix.years.quarters` was undefined, so `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize()` produced NaN. Use edit_file or a careful sed; verify with `cd /luxon && git diff src/duration.js` that the only changes are the two added `quarters: 4,` lines plus the previously added `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60,` line in casualMatrix.quarters (that one is already there and must stay).

STEP 2 (verification, after the edit): write /tmp/verify_q.js and run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/verify_q.js`. Import `const { Duration } = require("/luxon/src/luxon.js");`. For every ordered pair (a, b) of ["years","quarters","months","weeks","days","hours","minutes","seconds","milliseconds"] (including a === b), build `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1 })`, call `.normalize()`, and require that EVERY value in `.toObject()` is finite (not NaN) and that `.as("milliseconds")` equals the un-normalized duration's `.as("milliseconds")` within a relative tolerance of 1e-9. Print every failing pair and a total failure count (must be 0). Repeat the loop with `Duration.fromObject({ [a]: 1, [b]: 1, conversionAccuracy: "longterm" })` (note: conversionAccuracy must be INSIDE the object) and print that failure count (must be 0). Also print `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize().toObject()`, `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1 }).as("quarters")` (expect 4), `Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("years")` (expect 0.25), and `Duration.fromObject({ years: 1, quarters: 1 }).normalize().toObject()` for longterm.

STEP 3: run `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 20` and report the numbers and the exact names of any failing tests. Expected: 894 tests, 892 passing, and the ONLY failures are the two pre-existing French-locale ones in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js (`DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds`). Any other failing test is a regression and must be reported loudly.

REPORT: the git diff of src/duration.js, the two failure counts and any failing pair lines, the explicit values, and the jest numbers with failing test names.

Final end-to-end verification in the JS repo at /luxon. Treat the repo as READ-ONLY (do not edit anything in /luxon); put scratch files in /tmp. Use bash/read_file. Be quick and precise.

1) `cd /luxon && git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` and `git diff --stat`. Report both. Confirm that ONLY these source files are modified and that NO test file (anything under test/) is modified or added: src/interval.js, src/impl/util.js, src/datetime.js, src/duration.js, src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js.
2) `cd /luxon && git diff` — report the complete diff verbatim (it should be small).
3) Write /tmp/final_check.js and run `cd /luxon && npx babel-node /tmp/final_check.js`. It must import `const { DateTime, Duration, Interval, Settings, FixedOffsetZone } = require("/luxon/src/luxon.js");` and check each of these expected behaviours, printing PASS/FAIL for each:
   a) Settings.throwOnInvalid = true; Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00/2008-05-11T15:30:00").isValid === true; Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M").isValid === true; Interval.fromISO("P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00").isValid === true; Interval.fromISO("2007-03-01T13:00:00/hello") throws; Interval.fromISO("hello/2008-05-11T15:30:00") throws; Interval.fromISO("hello") throws; Interval.fromISO(null) throws. Then Settings.throwOnInvalid = false; and Interval.fromISO("hello").isValid === false.
   b) DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31", { zone: "utc" }).plus({ days: 61 }).toISODate() === "0100-03-02"; plus({days: 60}) === "0100-03-01"; plus({days: 62}) === "0100-03-03"; DateTime.fromISO("0100-01-02", { zone: "utc" }).minus({ days: 2 }).toISODate() === "0099-12-31".
   c) For zone "America/New_York", every day from 1974-01-06 to 1974-10-27 at hour 12 has isInDST === true (count the violations; must be 0); 1974-01-05 is false; 1974-10-28 is false; and for 2016: Jan 15 false, Jul 15 true, Dec 15 false.
   d) Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }).normalize().toObject() deep-equals { quarters: 1, seconds: 1 }; Duration.fromObject({ quarters: 1 }).as("seconds") === 7862400; Duration.fromObject({ seconds: 1 }).shiftTo("quarters").quarters is finite and > 0.
   e) DateTime.fromObject({ year: -10, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate() === "-0010-05-25"; DateTime.fromObject({ year: -118040, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate() === "-118040-05-25"; DateTime.fromObject({ year: 118040, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate() === "+118040-05-25"; DateTime.fromObject({ year: 1982, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc" }).toISODate() === "1982-05-25".
   f) new FixedOffsetZone("blorp").isValid === false; FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp").isValid === false; DateTime.fromMillis(0, { zone: FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp") }).isValid === false and its invalidReason === "unsupported zone"; FixedOffsetZone.utcInstance.isValid === true; FixedOffsetZone.instance(-300).name === "UTC-5".
   Print a final count of PASS/FAIL lines.
4) Run the full test suite: `cd /luxon && npx jest 2>&1 | tail -n 12`. Report the numbers and the names of the failing tests. The only acceptable failures are the two pre-existing ones in test/datetime/toFormat.test.js: `DateTime#toFormat('FFF') returns a medium date/time representation without seconds` and `DateTime#toFormat('FFFF') returns a long date/time representation without seconds` (French locale, "9:23:54" vs "09:23:54").

REPORT: git status/diff, the complete diff, every PASS/FAIL line plus the final counts, and the full-suite numbers with failing test names.
